## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Cūḷasugandhattheraapadāna* is a canonical verse text preserved within the *Therāpadāna* collection of the Sutta Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Belonging to the biographical and devotional tradition of early Buddhist verse, it relates the past meritorious deeds and spiritual lineage of the elder Cūḷasugandha. SuttaCentral documents five modern translations across five languages [SuttaCentral]. No dedicated discussion or analytical treatment of this text appears in the surveyed secondary literature corpus.

According to DharmaNexus automated analysis, the text exhibits significant Pali-internal textual reuse across 38 texts with 148 matching passages [DharmaNexus]. A large continuous section of the poem (§§0.3–34.4) is directly cited or preserved in the commentary to the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, Dutiyo bhāgo) [DharmaNexus]. Portions of the narrative are also shared with the *Pakiṇṇaka-gantha-saṅgaho Rasavāhinī* (§§7.2–16.4) and the closely named *Sugandhattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 532, §§0.2–4.4) [DharmaNexus]. Standard apadāna formulae, particularly in the concluding segments (§§35.1–41.1), align with numerous other poems in the collection, such as the *Vanavacchattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 551), *Paṭācārātherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 20), and *Mogharājattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 542) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also generates machine matches with Tibetan canonical works, including the *Ārya-dānapāramitā-sūtra* (D0182) and the *Tathāgatasaṃgīti-sūtra* (D0229), as well as the Chinese *Bieyi za ahan jing* (T 100), though these alignments reflect thematic phrase parallels rather than curated historical parallels [DharmaNexus].
